newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end slightly up, mirror Dow 30.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end slightly up, mirror Dow 30.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly higher, helped by firm Wall Street stock prices, but trading was limited on a lack of local market-moving news, brokers said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares closed up 0.76 percent at 63,828 points.
Volume was a moderate 282 million reais (US$276.7 million), below the recent daily average volume of 400 million reais.
Investors' expectations that a hike in U.S. short-term interest rates, if it happens, will not be as strong as previously thought helped to boost market sentiment, analysts said.
Some traders said the market could continue moving higher on positive expectations of a Senate vote Thursday on a bill exempting exports from the so-called ICMS tax.

The bill, already approved by the Chamber of Deputies, will have a positive impact on export companies, including mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce VAL_p.SA VAL.SA and steel firms Cosipa and CSN.
But they discounted the possibility of a strong rally caused by the ICMS tax vote.
Benchmark Telebras preferred ended up 0.97 percent at 77.85 reais, while the firm's common stock rose 0.43 percent to close at 62.75 reais.
Vale do Rio Doce preferred rose 0.73 percent, ending at 20.65 reais. State oil company Petrobras preferred rose 2.07 percent to end at 122.99 reais.
Sao Paulo bourse's Energy Electrical Sector (IEE) fell 0.2 percent, ending at 1,592 points.
